**Recent Polls (last 3 weeks)**

- Oct 29, 2026 – ActiVote: Talarico leads Paxton by 4.2%, widened from 2.0% in the Oct 21 poll. https://www.activote.net
- Oct 26-28 – Quantus Insights: 48.7% backed Paxton, while 47.6% backed Talarico. https://www.fox7austin.com
- Oct 27-Nov 1 – NYT/Siena: Talarico a 7-point advantage with 50% to Paxton's 43%, surveying 1,215 likely voters. https://www.newsweek.com
- Oct 28-Nov 1 – AtlasIntel: Talarico received 51.3% compared with 45.4% for Paxton, a 5.9-point lead. https://www.newsweek.com

**Assessment**: Polling averages and ratings suggest a genuine toss-up leaning slightly Democratic, with most late polls (6 of 8 above) showing Talarico ahead by 1-7 points, though the state's deep GOP lean and a few tied/Paxton-favoring polls introduce real uncertainty.

## Maine Senate 2026: Troy Jackson (D) vs. Susan Collins (R) — Research Summary

**Candidates & context**
- Republican incumbent Susan Collins is seeking a sixth term, challenged by Democratic former state Senate president Troy Jackson. Jackson became the nominee after Sullivan harbor master Graham Platner won the primary but withdrew July 10 amid sexual assault accusations; Jackson was chosen via nominating convention on July 25. (Wikipedia, accessed Nov 3, 2026)

**State lean/history**
- Maine is considered moderately blue; it has voted Democratic for president since 1992, and Harris beat Trump by ~7 points in 2024. This is the only Republican-held Senate seat in a state Trump lost in 2024. In 2020, Democrat Sara Gideon led every public poll before Election Day, yet Collins won by nearly 9 points—one of the worst polling misses nationally.

**Recent polls (last 3 weeks)**
- **WaPo-Schar School (Sept 30–Oct 5):** Jackson 50%, Collins 46%, among 800 likely voters.
- **YouGov (Oct 1):** Tied at 50%.
- **Marist (Oct 1–4):** Jackson 49%, Collins 47%.
- **CNN/SSRS:** Jackson 49%, Collins 45%.
- **Data for Progress:** Jackson 50%, Collins 45%.
- **YouGov (Oct 26–29):** Jackson 52%, Collins 47%, among 1,503 likely voters.
- **University of New Hampshire (Oct 27–31):** Jackson 54%, Collins 45%, 1,722 likely voters, MoE ±2.4.
- **NYT/Portland Press Herald/Siena (Oct 27–Nov 1, final):** Jackson 51%, Collins 45%, 714 likely voters, MoE 4.3% — a nine-point swing from September's version.
- Note: A Trafalgar poll gave Collins a fractional advantage; Collins has not led a public poll since late September.

**Perception vs. polls:** Despite Jackson's strongest polling, 56% of UNH likely voters said Collins will win Tuesday vs. 26% for Jackson.

**Ratings:** Cook Political Report rates it a "Toss Up."

**Fundraising:** Nearly $50 million raised by the campaigns combined, with almost $150 million spent by outside groups. Jackson has outraised Collins roughly four-to-one via small ActBlue donors; Collins has more cash on hand plus heavier outside-group ad support.

**Election Day news (Nov 2-3):** Early voting in Maine increased sharply vs. 2022, with registered Democrats at 47% of ballots cast vs. 23% Republican through Sunday. This race could decide Senate control.
